title: Build a typed service locator that fails fast

task.text: A service locator hands out services by type. Make it strict, so a missing service shows up at startup, not on a customer's request.
`Mailer` is given. Implement the two skeletons.

items: `ServiceLocator.register(Class<T>, T)` stores a service. Registering a type twice throws `IllegalStateException("already registered: Mailer")`, also under concurrent calls.
`ServiceLocator.get(Class<T>)` throws `IllegalStateException("no service registered for Mailer")` when absent. Names are simple class names.
Each `ServiceLocator` has its own services; nothing is static.
`SignupService(ServiceLocator)` looks the `Mailer` up in its constructor, not in `signUp`; `signUp(email)` sends the body `Welcome`.

checks.title: A missing service fails with a clear message
A missing Mailer fails when SignupService is built
register checks and stores in one atomic step

hints.text: A locator is a map from type to instance. Two rules make it safe: be strict about what you register and what you hand out, and let consumers resolve what they need as early as possible.

Back `ServiceLocator` with an instance `ConcurrentHashMap<Class<?>, Object>`. Use `putIfAbsent` so two racing threads cannot both win. `SignupService` keeps a `private final Mailer` set in its constructor.
